newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Stocks to list hotel unit, enter gaming bids. [CORRECTED 15:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Stocks to list hotel unit, enter gaming bids. [CORRECTED 15:05 GMT]

text.p: Construction group Stocks & Stocks Ltd said on Thursday its hotels and resorts division will be listed separately on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) in mid-February with an initial market capitalisation of 250 million rand. (Corrects month of listing from March to mid-February.)

Bart Dorrestein, chief executive officer of the group said the listing on the JSE's hotels, beverages and leisure sector will raise 110 million rand of new capital from institutional investors who have been invited to take a 45 percent slice.

Dorrestein declined to identify the institutions but said there was a black empowerment element to the deal. "There are a number of institutions that we are involved with...I think we can say that it has been very well received," he said.
The firm said an announcement on new equity partners in Stocks Hotels & Resorts, in which Stocks will retain the remaining 55 percent stake, would be made in about 10 days time.
Stocks on Thursday released results for the six months to end October with attributable income up a flat four percent to 16.01 million rand on steady turnover of 823.8 million.
Blaming slower-than-expected economic growth, Dorrestein said Stocks would show earnings growth in the second six months.
"Our real growth last year was 25 percent...We will have growth this year but we will not be able to maintain that."
Dorrestein said the separate listing would strengthen the hotel unit's balance sheet and allow it to focus on its own concerns, of which bidding for gambling licenses was key.
Bids would be made for 10 licenses, focussing on the Western Cape province. Excluding the boon of securing a license, the hotels unit expected earnings to grow by some 25 percent a year.
"The growth path for the hotels are set but the real bonanza will be the granting of these gambling licenses...That's where we see the growth in the leisure industry," he said.

Legislation last year legalised gambling in South Africa for the first time. Forty licences are up for grabs in an industry worth an estimated four billion rand a year, but provinces, which hold the reins, have been slow to set up the necessary infrastructure.

Stocks on Thursday also unveiled plans to unbundle and restructure its property division later this year. A company spokeswoman said a separate vehicle would be created to hold its interests and equity partners may be brought in although Stocks would retain control. A separate listing was not ruled out.
"We have positioned both companies for the growth we anticipate in the leisure and gaming markets as well as the construction sectors," Dorrestein said.

Turning to the group's other divisions, he said Stocks had received a 450 million rand boost to its order book in the last few weeks, including winning a 165 million rand contract to extend buildings at Johannesburg International Airport.
Stocks in December was part of the consortium which was awarded a major 3.5 billion rand contract to upgrade the road between Gauteng province and the Mozambican capital of Maputo.

"Maputo means about 600 million rand in turnover for Stocks over the next three years," chairman Reg Edwards said, adding, however, that the project would only start generating income in the second half of the 1997/98 financial year.
